title: Cost of the Nest, the Saratoga and the Cotton Club versus the Savoy
summary: The Nest and Saratoga were small, expensive cabarets, while the Cotton Club catered to movie stars; Holmes wishes for a Savoy in every borough.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What about the Saratoga Club and the Nest?

Well, that was a.... Well, the Nest was a little cabaret; a little small cabaret. It didn't hold too many people. But the Saratoga was... Well, that was a small cabaret, too. They didn't draw people like the Savoy did.
But there was dancing.

Well, you could dance, yeah. Anything your pocketbook could stand. You needed a little more cash to go in them places. At the Savoy, you could go in there for less than a dollar. But you didn't go in the Saratoga with
a dollar in your pocket. You would come out with your head beat in.
What did it cost to go to the Saratoga?
I don't know what it would cost to get out of there. It's just like any other club you go to. You go down to the Stork Club. How much it gonna cost to go to the Stork Club?
I see what you're saying.
Your drinks are high. Everything is high. Everything's high.
Was there an admission as well?
No, you just paid for...
You went and got a table.
That's right.
But there was a dance floor.
Oh yeah, there was a dance floor.
So generally, you ordered a bottle of something, I guess.
No, you ordered by the drink.
Oh, you ordered by the drink.
And that was higher. But that didn't go too good. They had a show down there, too.
So the clientele, then, at the Saratoga Club was also White?

Anyone who wanted could come in. They didn't do a good business, like the Cotton Club. Of course, they was almost directly across the street from the Cotton Club. But see, the Cotton Club catered to stars and things -- movie stars. That's what they catered to. I can't think of... I can see his name there. He knew everybody who was to be known. And they did a big business all through the...every night in the week. And they were also doing a lot of benefits and things. They were playing a lot of benefits.

Yeah, it was a well-run place. I mean, they knew what they were doing. It cost you plenty to go in there, or to come out -- one way or the other. You were going to spend a lot of money in the Cotton Club. At the Saratoga you wouldn't spend as much, but you would still spend more than if you was goin' to a place like the Savoy. You'd put that dollar down, and that's it -- and you could be in there for five or six hours or more, and be well entertained. The bands and the hostesses and one-thing-or-another in there... They had beautiful hostesses in there.

But see, they don't have all of that now to entertain the youth, take them off the streets, or this-that-and-the-other. And this city needs... They need a Savoy in every borough that they got here. Something for... I mean, a big

place to hold all these kids. Some place where they can go and be taught the right way to do things. It's a big deal, and... What can you say? It takes a lot of money? Everything takes a lot of money now. Youth, I think, is worth a lot of money. That's the future. They are your future senior citizens.
